# ferrotherm

> Thermodynamic computing in pure Rust: sparse energy-based models, chromatic block-Gibbs,
> parallel tempering, thermodynamic linear algebra, stochastic differentiable programs, a
> variational compiler onto device graph topologies, and a joules ledger pricing every operation
> against swappable device models. Zero dependencies, std-only, wasm-clean, deterministic by seed.
> Every module is verified against exact physics (Onsager 1944, exhaustive ground states,
> Gaussian elimination, finite-difference gradients) in `cargo test`.

Install: `cargo add ferrotherm` (or git: https://github.com/dcharlot-physicalai-bmi/ferrotherm)

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/dcharlot-physicalai-bmi/ferrotherm/blob/main/README.md): layer map, verification results, measured numbers with provenance labels
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/dcharlot-physicalai-bmi/ferrotherm/blob/main/AGENTS.md): invariants, task recipes, contribution rules for AI agents
- [API docs](https://docs.rs/ferrotherm): module-level docs carry the math and its sources

## Start here if you are solving a problem, not studying a sampler

`model` is the layer most callers want. State a problem as variables with domains, constraints that
must hold, and an objective; it compiles to spins and answers in your own names. Everything below it
works in couplings and biases, which is the machine's language rather than the problem's.

Values are the modeller's own values everywhere, never slot indices: an integer over 10..=20 takes
the value 13, and 3 is an error naming the range. `feasible` means every variable decoded AND every
constraint held; when it is false, `violated` names what was broken and `did_not_decode` names the
variables whose encoding lost. A penalty makes a constraint expensive, not impossible.

Reachable from Rust, C (include/ferrotherm.h), Python (python/ferrotherm), wasm, the node editor,
an HTTP API and an MCP server. Zig and Julia currently bind the spin layer only.

## Key modules

- model: variables, constraints (not_equal, equal, fix, cardinality, at_most, at_least, exactly-one,
  at-most-one), linear and quadratic objectives; compiles to spins, decodes by name, checks itself
- encode: one-hot, binary and domain-wall encodings of a categorical variable
- certify: what a run ACTUALLY did, computed from its samples -- effective beta, ESS, integrated
  autocorrelation time, TV from the exact distribution beside the sampling noise floor
- ftp: the portable program format every backend reads (spec/ftp-v1.md is normative)
- exact, planted, oracle: answers known before the machine is asked -- variable elimination, planted
  ground states, and a solver trait including one that exists to fail
- fabric, conform: what a device can do, and a conformance suite that can reject a machine
- graph, gibbs: sparse pairwise EBMs, chromatic block-Gibbs with clamping
- device: published degree-16 grid topology of Z1-class thermodynamic chips
- ledger: joules accounting (samples/reads/writes x device Prices; Z1_SPICE = vendor pre-silicon estimates)
- tempering: simulated annealing + parallel tempering (replica exchange), ladder-health diagnostics
- tla: thermodynamic linear algebra (OU network solves SPD systems, samples N(A^-1 b, A^-1/beta))
- program: stochastic differentiable circuits; REINFORCE + parameter-shift + FD-referee gradients
- compile: variational compilation of conditionals onto device patches; chain-rule KL error bound
- ffi: C ABI (ft_*) for wasm and host languages, including the whole modelling layer (ft_model_*)

## Examples (each is a verification gate, exit code = pass/fail)

- ring_tv, onsager: sampler vs exact Boltzmann / Onsager closed form
- z1_ledger: generative vs 100 Hz control regimes priced at vendor SPICE costs
- grad_check, gibbs_grad, lqr_energy: gradient cross-validation; trained controller vs provable optimum
- compile_chain, reach_on_z1: compilation error bound verified exactly; the control-workload boundary
- flips_bench: CPU throughput anchor

## Servers, for an agent

- `ferrotherm-serve`: an HTTP API and an MCP server over the same operations. Six MCP tools; reach
  for `ferrotherm_solve` first, since every other tool wants a graph of spins and returns an array
  of +/-1. `GET /v1/capabilities` describes the HTTP side.
- The node editor exposes `window.ferrotherm` for scripted use: `ready`, `types()`, `add`, `set`,
  `connect`, `find`, `run()`, `toJson`/`fromJson`, `check()`. See web-tests/editor.test.mjs, which
  drives exactly that surface.

## Live

- In-browser instrument (verifies vs Onsager on YOUR GPU, then measures): https://energy.physicalai-bmi.org/thermo
- Node editor: https://energy.physicalai-bmi.org/assets/ferrotherm/graph.html
